note: Rift shoulders: the ground around the basin is lifted, keeping its own relief and fading into the continent
The highland plateau behind the escarpment, rising toward the central range; raised over the existing ground so it keeps natural relief
Large-scale rolling relief on the plateau so it reads as highland, not a table

Escarpment top: the plateau's raised lip along the basin, highest where it breaks off; its steep face runs on south-west along the Caravan pass to the pass mouth, so the pass is a defile and not a way up onto the plateau (P29)
Natural roughness on the escarpment and rims

East block: a narrow horst on the basin's east side (the Danakil Alps' role), with spurs falling away eastward; its inner face steps in and out (two re-entrants for fans, one spur) instead of running ruler-straight (G3, A1)
East horst, north segment: a lower block where the horst runs into the north fault block, so the two are separate steps and not one ramp (crests vary by fault segment, G3)
East horst, south segment: a lower block stepped back from the middle one (G3)
South rim, west segment: the higher fault block, inner face at about y 0.90 (G3, A1)
South rim, east segment: a lower block stepped back about 4 km south of the west one (en echelon, G3, A1)
Relay ramp where the two south-rim segments overlap: a saddle in the crest, still above the Caravan pass so the basin stays closed (G3, G29)
Broken relief on the outer slopes of the rims and shoulders
Falls stream valley, upper plateau: graded so the stream runs downhill from its source to the falls (G7, G13); the head of the city's climb onto the plateau (P28)
Falls stream valley, mid plateau
Falls stream valley, cut through the escarpment's raised lip
Falls stream valley, the notch above the gorge (the falls has cut back into the scarp, G13)
Basin floor: an irregular rift trough carved into the shoulders, sharp along the escarpment; its south and east edges follow the offset rim segments and re-entrants (A1)
Caravan Approach, outer limb: falls from the col to the lowland
Caravan Approach, inner limb: falls from the col to the basin floor
Caravan Approach: the one low pass through the south-west rim; its col (400 m) is the basin's lowest exit, with the ground falling both ways (G29, P-b)
Terrace at the escarpment's foot: the Slums' ground, on the fan below the falls
Upper-city shelf: a bench cut into the escarpment just east of the gorge, directly overlooking the Slums, at the head of the only graded climb onto the plateau (P21, P28)

Falls gorge, head, below the notch: the stream's cut through the escarpment steps down in cascades with no uphill step (G7, G13), and the road climbs beside it: the only graded climb from the basin onto the plateau (P28)

Falls gorge, beside the upper-city shelf (the city's intake): the stream's cut through the escarpment steps down in cascades with no uphill step (G7, G13), and the road climbs beside it: the only graded climb from the basin onto the plateau (P28)

Falls gorge, middle: the stream's cut through the escarpment steps down in cascades with no uphill step (G7, G13), and the road climbs beside it: the only graded climb from the basin onto the plateau (P28)

Falls gorge, mouth, where the falls drop to the Slums: the stream's cut through the escarpment steps down in cascades with no uphill step (G7, G13), and the road climbs beside it: the only graded climb from the basin onto the plateau (P28)
Escarpment bench south of the Slums terrace: the master fault steps down in two (G2, A5)
Escarpment bench on the Caravan pass's north-west wall: a second fault step between the pass and the plateau (G2, A5)

Dead Spring hollow: a shallow fan-toe hollow well above the pan, so its pools never tie the brine pools (P19, G10, G12)

North rim, raised into one fault block from the plateau's east edge past the volcano to the east horst, merging north into the central range's foothills. Drawn after the basin carve with a sharp edge so its south face is a continuous scarp with no graded way up: the city's ramp is the only practical climb onto the plateau (P29, P28; G1-G2)
Relief on the north fault block, kept above its scarp foot (clamped) so the scarp stays a scarp

Active volcano: a cone built as stacked concentric sets drawn in km, replacing the flat table and its 2 km lava-lake shaft (A3, G4, G34). It stands on the north fault block, whose scarp is its steep foot (r 7.5 km), so the cone gives no graded way up onto the rim (P29); a tall lone stratovolcano off the rift axis is a recorded look choice from the vault's layout (P18, P8). The summit lava lake is the marker's note, not a pit (sub-cell, G34)

Smooths the cone inside its foot (not the foot itself, so its scarp stays sharp) so it reads as one cone, not stacked rings (A3, G34)
